nodes.name: Daily Check (09:00 UTC)
nodes.notes: Breadth data only changes when you post a new week's report (whenever that happens to land), so a daily poll is enough to catch a new week's signals within 24h. This never re-sends the same signal — the alerts_sent table (checked further down) dedupes per (week_of, category), so polling more or less often only changes how quickly you hear about a new week, not whether you get spammed.

nodes.name: Get Latest Week
nodes.notes: Reads v_scorecard_wow (defined in supabase_schema.sql) for the most recent week that has a complete row for at least one category. If nothing has been ingested yet, this returns zero rows and the whole chain below simply does nothing — no error, no alert.

nodes.name: Get Scorecard Rows
nodes.notes: Every category's scorecard row for the latest week — score, call, and the week-over-week deltas computed by v_scorecard_wow. Branches directly off 'Get Latest Week' (not off a downstream multi-item node) so this only fires once, not once per category.

nodes.name: Get Already Alerted
nodes.notes: Which categories already have a row in alerts_sent for this same week_of — i.e. already got a Telegram message. Also branches directly off 'Get Latest Week' so it runs exactly once, in parallel with Get Scorecard Rows.

nodes.name: Tag: scorecard
nodes.notes: Marks each item's origin so the merged list downstream can tell scorecard rows from already-alerted rows apart.

nodes.name: Tag: alerted
nodes.notes: Same tagging for the already-alerted-categories branch.

nodes.name: Merge
nodes.notes: Append mode: concatenates the two tagged lists into one input for Detect New Alerts (NOT position/key matching — the two branches are different lengths in general, so append is the only mode that's correct here). Order doesn't matter downstream — the next node splits by __kind.

nodes.name: Detect New Alerts
nodes.notes: Regex-free diff logic, tested standalone (node detect_new_alerts.js) against synthetic rows covering: a regime flip, a big score swing with no call change, a category with no signal, and a category that's already in alerts_sent (must be suppressed even though it also has a fresh volatility flag). Same thresholds as scorecard.py / v_scorecard — see the comment in supabase_schema.sql about keeping them in sync. Outputs zero items when nothing new crossed a threshold, which quietly ends the chain below (no message sent).

nodes.name: Build Telegram Message
nodes.notes: Combines however many categories triggered into one message (Telegram-friendly Markdown). Branches off Detect New Alerts alongside Record Alerts Sent — this node's output doesn't gate that one, so a category is recorded as alerted regardless of whether the Telegram send itself succeeds (see README-n8n.md for why, and the tradeoff that implies).

nodes.name: Send Telegram Alert
nodes.notes: Plain Bot API call (not n8n's Telegram node) so setup stays consistent with the rest of this pipeline: just two env vars, no separate credential to configure in the n8n UI. Needs TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (from @BotFather) and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID (your own chat id with that bot) set on the n8n host. Not live-tested from this session — no bot token to test against — see README-n8n.md for how to verify it once.

nodes.name: Record Alerts Sent
nodes.notes: Runs once per newly-alerted category (default 'once per input item' behaviour — deliberately not runOnceForAllItems here, unlike the Code nodes). Upsert on (week_of, category) so a re-run the same day is harmless. This is what makes tomorrow's poll skip these same categories.
